entries.a_ar: نسمّي التكامل $I$. بالتعويض $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$ نجد أيضاً $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\cos x)\,dx=I$. وبالجمع: $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin x\cos x)\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln\!\big(\tfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\big)dx=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx$. وبالتعويض $u=2x$ في التكامل الأخير نحصل على $\tfrac12\int_0^{\pi}\ln(\sin u)\,du=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin u)\,du=I$ (بالتناظر حول $\pi/2$). إذن $2I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+I$، ومنه $I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2$.
entries.a_en: Call the integral $I$. By the substitution $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$, $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\cos x)\,dx=I$ as well. Adding, $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin x\cos x)\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln\!\big(\tfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\big)dx=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx$. Substituting $u=2x$ in the last integral gives $\tfrac12\int_0^{\pi}\ln(\sin u)\,du=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin u)\,du=I$ (by symmetry about $\pi/2$). Hence $2I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+I$, so $I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2$.

entries.a_ar: لنضع $I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\ln(1+\tan x)\,dx$ ونطبّق التعويض $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{4}-x$. بما أنّ $\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x)=\tfrac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}$ فإنّ $1+\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x)=\tfrac{2}{1+\tan x}$. ومنه $I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\big[\ln 2-\ln(1+\tan x)\big]dx=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2-I$. إذن $2I=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2$، فيكون $I=\tfrac{\pi}{8}\ln 2$.
entries.a_en: Let $I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\ln(1+\tan x)\,dx$ and apply $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{4}-x$. Since $\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x)=\tfrac{1-\tan x}{1+\tan x}$, we get $1+\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-x)=\tfrac{2}{1+\tan x}$. Thus $I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\big[\ln 2-\ln(1+\tan x)\big]dx=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2-I$. Therefore $2I=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2$, giving $I=\tfrac{\pi}{8}\ln 2$.

entries.a_ar: لنضع $I=\int_0^{\pi}\frac{x\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx$. باستخدام $x\to \pi-x$ (حيث يبقى $\sin x$ و$\cos^2 x$ دون تغيير) نجد $I=\int_0^{\pi}\frac{(\pi-x)\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx=\pi\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx-I$. إذن $2I=\pi\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx$. وبالتعويض $u=\cos x$ نحصل على $\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{du}{1+u^2}=[\arctan u]_{-1}^{1}=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$، فيكون $2I=\pi\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ ومنه $I=\tfrac{\pi^2}{4}$.
entries.a_en: Let $I=\int_0^{\pi}\frac{x\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx$. Using $x\to \pi-x$ (so $\sin x$ and $\cos^2 x$ are unchanged), $I=\int_0^{\pi}\frac{(\pi-x)\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx=\pi\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx-I$. Hence $2I=\pi\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}\,dx$. Substituting $u=\cos x$ gives $\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{du}{1+u^2}=[\arctan u]_{-1}^{1}=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $2I=\pi\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $I=\tfrac{\pi^2}{4}$.

entries.q_ar: المنطقة المحدودة بالمنحنى $y=\ln x$ ومحور السينات والمستقيم $x=e$ تدور حول محور الصادات. أوجد حجم المجسّم الناتج.
entries.q_en: The region bounded by $y=\ln x$, the $x$-axis, and the line $x=e$ is revolved about the $y$-axis. Find the volume of the resulting solid.
entries.a_ar: تمتدّ المنطقة على $1\le x\le e$ بارتفاع $y=\ln x\ge 0$. باستخدام طريقة القشور الأسطوانية حول محور الصادات: $V=\int_1^{e} 2\pi x\,\ln x\,dx$. وبالتكامل بالتجزئة مع $u=\ln x,\ dv=x\,dx$: $\int x\ln x\,dx=\tfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\tfrac{x^2}{4}$. وبالتعويض من $1$ إلى $e$: $\big(\tfrac{e^2}{2}-\tfrac{e^2}{4}\big)-\big(0-\tfrac14\big)=\tfrac{e^2}{4}+\tfrac14=\tfrac{e^2+1}{4}$. إذن $V=2\pi\cdot\tfrac{e^2+1}{4}=\tfrac{\pi(e^2+1)}{2}$.
entries.a_en: The region runs over $1\le x\le e$ with height $y=\ln x\ge 0$. Using cylindrical shells about the $y$-axis, $V=\int_1^{e} 2\pi x\,\ln x\,dx$. Integrating by parts with $u=\ln x,\ dv=x\,dx$: $\int x\ln x\,dx=\tfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\tfrac{x^2}{4}$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $\big(\tfrac{e^2}{2}-\tfrac{e^2}{4}\big)-\big(0-\tfrac14\big)=\tfrac{e^2}{4}+\tfrac14=\tfrac{e^2+1}{4}$. Thus $V=2\pi\cdot\tfrac{e^2+1}{4}=\tfrac{\pi(e^2+1)}{2}$.

entries.a_ar: لنضع $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}$ حيث $a=\sqrt2$. نطبّق التعويض $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$ الذي يحوّل $\tan x\to\cot x=1/\tan x$: $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+(\tan x)^{-a}}=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{(\tan x)^{a}}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}\,dx$. وبجمع الصيغتين: $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{1+(\tan x)^{a}}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}dx=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$. إذن $I=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$، وهي قيمة مستقلة عن الأُسّ $a$.
entries.a_en: Let $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}$ with $a=\sqrt2$. Apply $x\to \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$, which sends $\tan x\to\cot x=1/\tan x$: $I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+(\tan x)^{-a}}=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{(\tan x)^{a}}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}\,dx$. Adding the two forms, $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{1+(\tan x)^{a}}{1+(\tan x)^{a}}\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}dx=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$. Hence $I=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$, independent of the exponent $a$.

entries.a_ar: نكتب $\frac{1}{x-1}=-\frac{1}{1-x}=-\sum_{n\ge 0}x^n$ عندما $0<x<1$، فيصبح المكامَل $-\sum_{n\ge0}x^n\ln x$. وبتبادل المجموع مع التكامل، ومع $\int_0^1 x^n\ln x\,dx=-\frac{1}{(n+1)^2}$، يصير التكامل $\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1}{k^2}$. وهذا هو $\zeta(2)=\frac{\pi^2}{6}$.
entries.a_en: Write $\frac{1}{x-1}=-\frac{1}{1-x}=-\sum_{n\ge 0}x^n$ for $0<x<1$, so the integrand equals $-\sum_{n\ge0}x^n\ln x$. Interchanging sum and integral, $\int_0^1 x^n\ln x\,dx=-\frac{1}{(n+1)^2}$, hence the integral is $\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{1}{(n+1)^2}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{1}{k^2}$. This is $\zeta(2)=\frac{\pi^2}{6}$.

entries.a_ar: لنسمِّ التكامل $I$ ونُدخل الوسيط $I(u)=\int_0^1 \frac{\arctan(u\sqrt{x^2+2})}{(x^2+1)\sqrt{x^2+2}}\,dx$ فيكون المطلوب $I(1)$. بالاشتقاق تحت علامة التكامل وتفكيك الكسور، يؤول الفرق $I(\infty)-I(1)$ إلى تكاملات قوس ظل ابتدائية؛ ومع $I(\infty)=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^1\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)\sqrt{x^2+2}}=\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi^2}{12}$ نحصل على الصيغة المغلقة الشهيرة. والنتيجة $\frac{5\pi^2}{96}$.
entries.a_en: Let $I$ be the integral and introduce $I(u)=\int_0^1 \frac{\arctan(u\sqrt{x^2+2})}{(x^2+1)\sqrt{x^2+2}}\,dx$ so the target is $I(1)$. Differentiating under the integral sign and using partial fractions, $I(\infty)-I(1)$ reduces to elementary arctangent integrals; combined with $I(\infty)=\frac{\pi}{2}\int_0^1\frac{dx}{(x^2+1)\sqrt{x^2+2}}=\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi^2}{12}$ one obtains the classical closed form. The result is $\frac{5\pi^2}{96}$.

entries.a_ar: لنسمِّ التكامل $I$. بالتعويض $x\mapsto \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$ نجد $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\cos x)\,dx=I$ أيضاً، إذن $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin x\cos x)\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln\!\big(\tfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\big)\,dx=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx$. وبالتعويض $t=2x$ يكون $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx=\tfrac12\int_0^{\pi}\ln(\sin t)\,dt=I$ (لتناظر الجيب حول $\pi/2$). فينتج $2I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln2+I$ ومنه $I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2$.
entries.a_en: Call the integral $I$. By $x\mapsto \tfrac{\pi}{2}-x$, $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\cos x)\,dx=I$ too, so $2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin x\cos x)\,dx=\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln\!\big(\tfrac{\sin 2x}{2}\big)\,dx=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx$. Substituting $t=2x$ gives $\int_0^{\pi/2}\ln(\sin 2x)\,dx=\tfrac12\int_0^{\pi}\ln(\sin t)\,dt=I$ (by symmetry of $\sin$ about $\pi/2$). Thus $2I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln2+I$, giving $I=-\tfrac{\pi}{2}\ln 2$.

entries.q_ar: أسطوانتان دائريتان قائمتان نصف قطر كلٍّ منهما $r$، ومحوراهما متعامدان ومتقاطعان. باستخدام التكامل، أوجد الحجم المضبوط للجسم المشترك بينهما (جسم شتاينمتز).
entries.q_en: Two right circular cylinders of radius $r$ have perpendicular, intersecting axes. Using integration, find the exact volume of the Steinmetz solid common to both cylinders.
entries.a_ar: لنأخذ الأسطوانتين $x^2+z^2\le r^2$ و $y^2+z^2\le r^2$. عند ارتفاع ثابت $z$ حيث $|z|\le r$، يعطي الشرطان $|x|\le\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$ و $|y|\le\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$، أي مقطعاً مربّعاً طول ضلعه $2\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$ ومساحته $4(r^2-z^2)$. إذن $V=\int_{-r}^{r}4(r^2-z^2)\,dz=4\big(2r^3-\tfrac{2r^3}{3}\big)=\frac{16}{3}r^3$.
entries.a_en: Take the cylinders $x^2+z^2\le r^2$ and $y^2+z^2\le r^2$. At a fixed height $z$ with $|z|\le r$, both conditions give $|x|\le\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$ and $|y|\le\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$, a square cross-section of side $2\sqrt{r^2-z^2}$ and area $4(r^2-z^2)$. Hence $V=\int_{-r}^{r}4(r^2-z^2)\,dz=4\big(2r^3-\tfrac{2r^3}{3}\big)=\frac{16}{3}r^3$.

entries.a_ar: نعوّض $x=\tan\theta$ فيصبح التكامل $J=\int_0^{\pi/4}\ln(1+\tan\theta)\,d\theta$. وباستعمال التحويل $\theta\mapsto \tfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta$ والمتطابقة $1+\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta)=\frac{2}{1+\tan\theta}$ نحصل على $J=\int_0^{\pi/4}\big[\ln 2-\ln(1+\tan\theta)\big]\,d\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2-J$. إذن $2J=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln2$ ومنه $J=\frac{\pi}{8}\ln 2$.
entries.a_en: Substitute $x=\tan\theta$, so the integral becomes $J=\int_0^{\pi/4}\ln(1+\tan\theta)\,d\theta$. Using $\theta\mapsto \tfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta$ and the identity $1+\tan(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\theta)=\frac{2}{1+\tan\theta}$, we get $J=\int_0^{\pi/4}\big[\ln 2-\ln(1+\tan\theta)\big]\,d\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln 2-J$. Hence $2J=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\ln2$, giving $J=\frac{\pi}{8}\ln 2$.
